themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 71 THIS WEEK, a 601% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 10.1 weekly complaints (z-score: 8.69), signaling a sudden, widespread deterioration in road infrastructure across Highbridge/Concourse.
evidence: 71 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (601% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically severe anomaly
Community Board has standing request to inspect/repair sanitary sewer on specific street segments, suggesting chronic infrastructure issues that may be accelerating
reporting_angles: Map which streets are most affected and interview residents about potholes, flooding, or damage
Investigate whether this spike correlates with recent heavy rain or deferred maintenance cycles
Contact NYC DOT for explanation and timeline for repairs

themes_detail.label: Sudden Spike in SPIT Enforcement
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% jump from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 complaints per week (z-score: 8.69), indicating either a concentrated enforcement campaign or sudden building/housing code violations in the district.
evidence: 3 SPIT complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically severe anomaly
336 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (210 alterations, 73 new buildings), suggesting active construction/renovation activity that may be triggering inspections
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings or addresses triggered SPIT inspections and what violations were cited
Interview residents or building owners about enforcement action and its scope
Determine if SPIT activity is tied to the 336 recent DOB filings or a separate compliance initiative

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints jumped to 29 THREE WEEKS AGO (510% above the 8-week baseline of 4.8 per week, z-score: 9.05), indicating a significant but now-slightly-aging spike in reported building/infrastructure maintenance failures across the district.
evidence: 29 maintenance/facility complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (510% spike)
Z-score of 9.05 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Overlaps with long-standing CB budget request for sewer inspection/repair and park building reconstruction, suggesting systemic maintenance backlogs
reporting_angles: Follow up on whether the spike from 3 weeks ago has subsided or if complaints continue to accumulate
Identify which city agencies own/maintain the facilities with the most complaints
Cross-reference with CB's repeated requests for sewer and park infrastructure investment to build narrative of deferred maintenance

themes_detail.label: Waste Collection & Sewer Issues
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints increased to 8 LAST WEEK (300% above the 8-week baseline of 2.0 per week, z-score: 3.62), while Missed Collection complaints rose to 6 (300% above 1.5 weekly average), signaling emerging sanitation infrastructure strain last week.
evidence: 8 sewer complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.62)
6 missed collection complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.4)
Community Board's standing request to inspect/repair sanitary sewer on specific streets aligns with rising sewer complaint trend
reporting_angles: Identify which streets are experiencing sewer backups or overflow issues and map geographic concentration
Investigate whether missed collections are citywide or specific to certain collection routes in Highbridge/Concourse
Interview DSNY and DEP about staffing, equipment shortages, or infrastructure failures driving the spike

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK, a 500% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.5 per week (z-score: 5.0), suggesting either a targeted city enforcement operation or complaints about unpermitted street vending in the district.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Community Board has standing request to 'support merchant organizing' via DSBS, indicating vendor/merchant community is a district priority
Spike suggests either enforcement action or merchant complaints about enforcement
reporting_angles: Determine whether spike reflects increased street vending complaints from residents or NYPD/DOC enforcement operations
Interview local vendors and community merchants about enforcement environment and their relationship with city agencies
Connect to CB's merchant organizing priority to understand whether enforcement is helping or hindering merchant community
